 Scottie Barnes scored 28 points (12-of- FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), fourteen rebounds, five assists, two steals, two blocks and a three on Friday.
 You would like Scottie to hit some more 3’s and not turn the ball over 8 times, but that’s not why you have him. These are the stat lines that you wanted when you drafted Scottie as early as you did. There are not many players that can get 28 points, 14 rebounds, and 5 assists in fantasy. Sit back and enjoy the high-level production.

 Scottie Barnes accounted for 23 points (8-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Wednesday was a record night in Toronto, as the Raptors broke last season’s mark for the largest season-opening win in franchise history. In the 135-92 rout of the Bulls, Barnes also moved into fifth on the franchise’s all-time assist list, passing Pascal Siakam. “Scottie B” was one of four Raptors starters to finish with at least 20 points, and he led the team in shot attempts (19). This sets up to be another big fantasy season for Barnes, especially with Kawhi Leonard making his return to Toronto. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes had 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, four blocks and four three-pointers in the exhibition against the Knicks on Thursday. 
 Barnes torched the Knicks’ backups for 19 points on Tuesday. With most of the Knicks’ starters playing Thursday, the results were pretty much the same for Barnes, who had another excellent game. The 25-year-old forward is a fantasy stud that can be had in the second round of drafts this year. 
 Scottie Barnes

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes lit up the Knicks with 19 points (8-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block on Tuesday. 
 If there was any concern about how Barnes would fit alongside Kawhi Leonard, he was able to quiet it with his performance in this game. Though it came against the Knicks’ backups, both players produced at a high level. Barnes has been a true fantasy star for most of his career and should continue to stuff the stat sheet despite Kawhi’s arrival. Managers should draft him early in the second round with confidence. 
 Scottie Barnes

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes accumulated 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds and three assists over 21 minutes in Saturday’s preseason game against the Clippers. 
 The Raptors didn’t make any significant offseason changes besides the Kawhi Leonard blockbuster, which should shift a considerable amount of the scoring burden away from Barnes this season. He made some tremendous strides from an efficiency standpoint last year and Leonard’s arrival should lead to even more favorable matchups on the offensive end of the floor. It’s worth noting that Leonard has yet to play this preseason, so we haven’t gotten a look at how the offense will run just yet. It took Barnes just over one half to record a double-double in this exhibition contest. He’s a borderline first-round pick in all fantasy drafts this fall.

 Scottie Barnes recorded 11 points (5-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and three steals in Saturday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 The Raptors didn’t need to push Barnes much in Saturday’s exhibition opener, so he spent the second half on the bench in street clothes. As usual, he did a little bit of everything during his 12 minutes on the floor. Barnes remains a highly valuable fantasy option regardless of league format, even with Kawhi Leonard’s return to Toronto. He should be no worse than a second-round pick in standard drafts.

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes tallied 24 points (8-of-14 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, one block and one three-pointer in the loss to the Cavaliers on Sunday. 
 Barnes was arguably Toronto’s best performer on Sunday. In his 37 minutes, efficient shooting led him to finish as the team’s top scorer, and his production on the defensive glass nearly led to a double-double. The fifth-year forward showcased his versatility on both ends of the floor and played well in essentially all seven games this series. He was virtually the same level of fantasy player this season as he was last. However, his success in the opening-round loss to the Cavaliers makes another leap in production in the 2026-27 season something fantasy managers could be optimistic about. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes finished Friday’s Game 6 win over the Cavaliers with 25 points (11-of-21 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, 14 assists, three steals and three blocks. 
 Barnes’ 14th assist of Game 6 was his most important, as a pass to RJ Barrett led to a three-pointer that gave Toronto a 112-110 lead with 1.2 seconds remaining in overtime. That shot would stand as the game-winner, sending the series back to Cleveland for a Game 7 on Sunday. Barnes, who finished Game 6 three rebounds shy of a triple-double, has been the best player in this series so far. And another performance like the one he produced on Friday will give Toronto a shot at advancing.

 Scottie Barnes (quad) is not on the injury report for Friday’s Game 6 against the Cavaliers. 
 Barnes played through a right quad contusion that he suffered during the second quarter of Wednesday’s Game 5 defeat. Following the game, he said that he’ll be fine for Game 6, and the Raptors have not even included Barnes on the initial injury report. With Toronto’s season on the line, Barnes will take on his usual workload, if not exceed it.

 Scottie Barnes (quad) recorded 17 points (6-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds, 11 assists, one steal and three blocks in Wednesday’s Game 5 loss to the Cavaliers. 
 Barnes may have recorded his second double-double of the series on Wednesday, but the Raptors’ star was not his usual self. He took a hit to the right quad during the second quarter and was hobbled the rest of the way, gutting out 39 minutes. When asked about the injury after the defeat, Barnes made it clear that he’ll be ready for Game 6 on Friday. The Raptors need a win to extend the series to a decisive Game 7, which would be played on Sunday in Cleveland.

 #4 
 Scottie Barnes totaled 23 points (6-of-15 FGs, 11-of-14 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, one steal and three blocks in the win over the Cavaliers on Sunday. 
 Both teams struggled to score in Sunday’s contest, but behind Barnes’ 23 points, the Raptors did just enough to win and even the series. The fifth-year forward earned nearly half of his points total at the charity stripe, with the remainder coming inside the three-point line. He tallied more rebounds and assists than any other Raptors player and was impactful on the defensive end of the floor. Now tied at two games apiece, the series flips back to Cleveland for Game 5, where Barnes will look to lead his team to a third straight victory.

 Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 28 points (10-of-18 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist, four steals and four three-pointers in a 125-121 loss to the Cavaliers on Saturday.
 Even if the Nets are going to struggle again this season, Porter is certainly going to get his buckets. He’ll have a good chance to lead the Nets in scoring, even if Julius Randle is a threat to that title. He was a fantasy stud last season, but through two games, he has been even better by becoming a strong source of steals with seven so far this year. That pace won’t continue, but he may be able to hover around one per game like he did last season.

 After totaling 19 points, 15 rebounds and seven assists in Milwaukee’s first two games, Kuzma recorded a double-double on Saturday.  Kel’el Ware produced 19 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 The past two days reminded everyone why Ware is such a frustrating player to roster in fantasy basketball. After a subpar showing in the Bucks’ loss to the Bulls on Friday, the 7-footer rebounded and produced his best effort of the season’s first week. Ware recorded a complete stat line against the 76ers, including his first double-double of the season. Meanwhile, starting center Myles Turner went scoreless, contributing just five rebounds, one assist and one block in 20 minutes. As a result, the team benched him during the fourth quarter, with Ware picking up those minutes.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Jaquez has started his first season in Milwaukee strong, scoring at least 19 points in each of his first three games. Against the 76ers, he shot over 50 percent from the field and added solid rebound and assist numbers. Jaquez has yet to record a steal or blocked shot this season, but the rebounding and offensive output have been good. Set to hit restricted free agency in the summer, Jaquez is well positioned to deliver top-100 value in category leagues.

 Nate Ament accounted for one point (1-of-4 FTs), three rebounds and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Ament made his official NBA debut on Saturday, and unfortunately, it didn’t go well. The rookie missed his lone field-goal attempt and shot 1-of-4 from the foul line, while also picking up five fouls in 11 minutes. Even without LeBron James, Philadelphia isn’t a good matchup for Ament at this stage in his career. But it’s something to build on, and he’ll have plenty of chances to make good on his perceived upside throughout the season.

 VJ Edgecombe amassed 17 points (5-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 On a night when Joel Embiid recorded a triple-double, Edgecombe posted his eighth career double-double. The 76ers guard shot 5-of-10 from beyond the arc, a welcome development after going 1-of-7 from deep in wins over the Knicks and Cavaliers. Given Philadelphia’s offensive firepower, Edgecombe will get plenty of catch-and-shoot opportunities, even on nights when the rotation isn’t whole. Consistently taking advantage of those chances should raise his fantasy ceiling.

 Tyrese Maxey recorded 26 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 Maxey finished the first and third quarters of Saturday’s win with buzzer-beaters, with one being a half-court shot. The 76ers’ point guard has scored at least 26 points in all three games this season, attempting 19 shots or more in each. Neither Maxey’s usage nor his production has suffered so far, and he’s especially well-positioned to feast in back-to-backs. LeBron James sat out Saturday’s game, and Joel Embiid won’t play on Sunday against the Pistons, which should be good news for those rostering Maxey.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brown did what he could to ensure that he’d celebrate a win on his 30th birthday, as he was one of three 76ers to score at least 26 points. According to NBC Sports Philadelphia, this is the first team JB has played on that has ranked in the top-10 in the league in pace.  Dean Wade finished Saturday’s win over the Bucks with seven points (2-of-3 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, three steals, one block and two three-pointers.
 After missing Philadelphia’s first two games with an ankle injury, Wade made his 76ers debut as a starter, stepping in for LeBron James (sciatica). The veteran forward produced solid value in steals, blocks and three-pointers, but more encouraging was Wade’s ability to play close to 30 minutes. The 76ers face Detroit on Sunday, and they may decide to sit Wade for injury management reasons. Consider him questionable for that one.
